# Process lessons from Cognition's RSA-260 factorization — what transfers to the RH program

**v1, Session 21, 2026-09-10.** Source: `page.md` in this folder (the post, Firecrawl scrape 2026-09-10); faithful account in `reader-report.md` beside it. Precedent for this kind of study: `results/external/openai-ns-2026/process-lessons.md` (the NS study), whose six-then-nine rules became `KICKSTART.md` Part 2 item 10 (a)–(j) (`KICKSTART.md` lines 67–78). Sponsor's question, verbatim: "check https://cognition.com/blog/factoring-rsa-260 for any insight in problem-solving that might be applicable to our RH program." This note is about METHOD; the factoring is recorded in the reader report and is not the point.

**Scale and kind disclaimer first.** The post describes a **computation**: a known algorithm ("GNFS is the most efficient algorithm known for (most) numbers above roughly 100 digits" — How did this happen?), a reference implementation ("CADO-NFS … provided all the relevant techniques, the pipeline stages and their interfaces, and a reference CPU implementation" — What did Devin still need me for?), and an answer checkable by one multiplication. It cost "about 4,900 GPU-days … about $400k" (Cost estimates) on "spare or fragmented compute" (Factoring on spare compute), with "an average of 3 and a maximum of 18 concurrent Devin sessions" over "3-week duration" (The optimization workflow). The RH program is a proof/refutation search under barriers (`BARRIER-ZOO.md`, 54 entries per `STATUS.md` line 118), run as "one workflow at a time; … at most two agents run side by side" (`STATUS.md` line 31; `KICKSTART.md` line 55), with the sponsor's charter that "a genuine proof of RH almost certainly requires entirely new mathematics" (`STATUS.md` line 32) and that "we must be really smart about directions to pursue" (`KICKSTART.md` line 67). Nothing below assumes the post's compute or width. What can transfer is how a human steered agents on a problem the human did not fully understand — which is, in one respect, this program's situation (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, "Do not ask Jay technical questions"), and in another respect its opposite (the sponsor wants new mathematics, not a faster known pipeline).

## The practices the post exhibits, one block each

### P1. Build the unified benchmarking framework first; it does not self-assemble.
*The page says:* "my biggest contribution was probably to handhold the creation of a unified set of measured results, benchmarks, and performance estimators, which evidently were not otherwise going to self-assemble. This enabled Devin to more easily run and understand measurements, and me to understand the extent of progress and where more improvements were needed" (What did Devin still need me for?). The corresponding instruction to the agents: "do measurements this way and find previous results here, don't cook up new incomparable approaches every time" (same section, item 5). The cost of not having it: "I wasted much search time on unproductive ranges due to incorrect benchmark interpretation" (Appendix 2, Polynomial selection); "643 GPU-days in polynomial selection (this is anomalously high basically due to operator incompetence)" (Cost estimates).
*What it is, in one sentence:* one fixed place and one fixed format in which every agent records comparable measurements and reads the previous ones, built before optimization starts and maintained by the human.
*Already adopted here?* Partly. 10(g) requires contract theorems, a constants dependency chain and a slack ledger (`KICKSTART.md` line 74); 10(a) requires an insights digest between phases (line 68); 10(e) gives each stream a `SHARED.md` (line 72). What is **not on the record** is a per-direction sheet of fixed, comparable measures that every unit must report in the same units — the program's equivalent of "find previous results here".
*Transfer to the RH program:* add to each `directions/*.md` a short "Instruments" table naming the direction's comparable quantities and their current best values with a pointer to the result file — e.g. for D1 the certified interval on Λ (currently "0 ≤ Λ ≤ 0.2", `STATUS.md` line 24) and the checker's label; for A4 the certified constant and the operating point; for the zoo the entry count and the Group IV count. Every brief must instruct the agent to report its numbers in that table's units and to append, not restate. Cost: a file section per direction, written once by the orchestrator; zero agents.
*Why it may NOT transfer:* a siever has one scalar (workunit seconds: "GB200s went from 585 s to 486s" — Appendix 2, Sieving) and every measurement is comparable by construction. A proof search has no scalar; the "measures" are certified bounds and counts, and a direction can be entirely healthy while none of them moves (the Grossmann sweep, `STATUS.md` line 34, produces fit judgments, not numbers). The risk is Goodhart: optimizing the instruments the sponsor has said are "instruments only" (`STATUS.md` line 32). So the table records, it never ranks.

### P2. Run up a scaling ladder with evenly spaced rungs; the post regrets the rung it skipped.
*The page says:* "For the first five days we ran up a scaling ladder. By the end of this, factoring a 190-digit number took the same amount of time as a 157-digit number had at the start — a little over 3 hours" (Running up the scaling ladder). The regret: "After factoring the C311 (which was roughly equivalent in difficulty to GNFS on a 216-digit number), it would have been safer to proceed by factoring a 230-digit equivalent difficulty number in order to cross the remaining couple of orders of magnitude. But I estimated that RSA-260 could be done in under a month and therefore had already begun polynomial selection, even though I knew the linear algebra remained significantly underoptimized" (same). The consequence the post records: "Optimization was turbulent because we simultaneously co-optimized matrix params, solver layout, and code targeting speculative final matrix properties" (Appendix 2, Linear algebra), and the final linear-algebra code "had not been tested on any smaller scale before starting the run" (same).
*What it is, in one sentence:* exercise the whole pipeline end-to-end on instances of increasing size, each within a stated factor of the last, and do not begin the target until the pipeline has run at the rung below it.
*Already adopted here?* Yes, 10(b): new machinery is first run "on the rungs where the answer is KNOWN — function fields (RH true), Epstein / Davenport–Heilbronn (RH false), then Dirichlet L … A brief that skips the ladder is returned" (`KICKSTART.md` line 69). What 10(b) does not say is (i) that the ladder is also a **dress rehearsal for the pipeline** (producers, checker, Lean build) and not only a test of the mathematics, and (ii) that the top rung must have been run **at the scale of the target** before the target starts.
*Transfer to the RH program:* sharpen 10(b) with the two clauses the post supplies: every computational leg (Lane A producers, D-R8-style Lean builds) runs end-to-end on a smaller instance of the same shape before the long run; and a brief that starts the target "even though … significantly underoptimized" on an estimate of feasibility is returned, as 10(b) already returns a brief that skips the ladder. Cost: two sentences in `KICKSTART.md`; zero agents (the rehearsal is a small run inside a stream already funded).
*Why it may NOT transfer:* GNFS has a difficulty scale ("standard GNFS scaling", Cost estimates) on which "230-digit equivalent" is a well-defined rung. Mathematics has no such scale: the function-field rung of a proof idea can be trivial and the ζ rung impossible, with no intermediate instance at all (the program's own C3-r record: the mapping-torus case closed, the Deninger leg "CLOSED at 'open in print'", `STATUS.md` line 24). The ladder can validate a pipeline; it cannot certify that the next rung exists.

### P3. A hierarchy of goals, tight scope, and redirection away from unproductive measurement.
*The page says:* "My role was primarily to set priorities, establish benchmarks, and recognize when work was going off-track" (opening, takeaway 2). The list: "setting a hierarchy of goals and keeping Devin properly scoped"; "recognizing when Devin was doing something unproductive and redirecting ('you don't need to take that measurement')" (What did Devin still need me for?, items 1–2). Cadence: "I interacted with this optimization loop once every couple of hours" (The optimization workflow). Two session types were kept distinct: "iteratively optimizing an individual component" and "managing end-to-end factorization runs … revealing the most important inefficiencies (errors, utilization, performance) for further optimization" (same).
*What it is, in one sentence:* the human owns the goal tree and the scope of each agent, and intervenes on a fixed cadence to kill work that does not serve the current node.
*Already adopted here?* Largely. The orchestrator writes every brief from `STATUS.md`'s queue (`STATUS.md` lines 115–121), sequential streams enforce one goal at a time (`STATUS.md` line 31), 10(d) reallocates on signal (`KICKSTART.md` line 71), and the Session 21 digest ranked the queue before any brief (`STATUS.md` line 116). **Not on the record:** a written *stop condition* in each brief — the agent-side form of "you don't need to take that measurement" — so that an agent working unattended for an hour can recognize off-track itself.
*Transfer to the RH program:* every brief carries one line "Stop and report when: …" naming the observation that makes the unit pointless (a source that says the lemma is already in print; a computation whose first slice contradicts the hypothesis; a rung of the ladder failing). Cost: one line per brief; zero agents. The post's two-session-type distinction maps to the program's builder/checker split (`STATUS.md` line 117, "builder + Opus checker") and needs no change.
*Why it may NOT transfer:* in the post, "unproductive" was decidable within hours from the benchmark. In the RH program a direction can look unproductive for sessions and be the right one — the Grossmann refinement says outright that "the absence of any published connection between a branch and ζ is never evidence against it" (`STATUS.md` line 34). Stop conditions must therefore be *factual* (a source found, a number computed), never *impressionistic* ("this seems not to be working"), or they would re-import the misreading the refinement forbids.

### P4. Catch premature give-up.
*The page says:* the sixth human role is "catching when Devin prematurely gave up on a direction" (What did Devin still need me for?). The post gives the example in reverse elsewhere: the square-root step failed and "Devin rebuilt `sqrt` three times (first using GMP's `mpn` functions and then also parallel Karatsuba on CPU); the version that ultimately produced the factors used GPU-accelerated NTT multiplication" (Appendix 2, Characters and square root).
*What it is, in one sentence:* an agent's report that a direction is dead is itself a claim to be checked, because agents abandon lines for reasons that are not obstructions.
*Already adopted here?* Half. 10(c) makes the refutation-shaped statement ("proof class X cannot yield Y because Z") every lane's default close and says "Barrier-zoo entries are extracted from these statements, not from prose" (`KICKSTART.md` line 70); standing order 5 forbids decisive action on unverified recalled claims (`STATUS.md` line 33). What is **not on the record** is the symmetric check at harvest: that a unit reported as failed was killed by a stated, re-derived obstruction and not by budget, fatigue, or a missing tool (the program has already caught the last kind once — standing order 9's trigger, `STATUS.md` line 37: a brief "had priced the Comparator run as blocked by the absence of Rust and Go").
*Transfer to the RH program:* at every harvest the orchestrator classifies each abandoned line as (i) obstruction stated and re-derived → zoo candidate, (ii) budget/tool/time → re-queue with the missing input named, or (iii) unexplained → one small re-run before it may be recorded as dead. Cost: a three-way label in the harvest entry in `LOG.md`; zero agents in cases (i)–(ii), one small agent in (iii).
*Why it may NOT transfer:* in factoring, giving up is almost always wrong because the answer exists and the pipeline is known to reach it. In this program the barrier zoo *is* the durable asset ("the zoo's Group IV … is the compounding asset", NS study line 52), and a correct give-up — a proved obstruction — is a result, not a failure. So the rule cannot be "persist"; it has to be "name the obstruction or name the missing input", which is why it is written symmetrically above.

### P5. Recognize repeated inefficiencies and amortize setup.
*The page says:* the third human role is "recognizing repeated inefficiencies in Devin's workflows ('you can amortize this setup work')" (What did Devin still need me for?). The post's own amortized setup was the platform: "sessions are persistent and independent from my computer … sessions can run autonomously for weeks" (The optimization workflow).
*What it is, in one sentence:* setup that every agent repeats is moved into a shared prelude once, by the human.
*Already adopted here?* Yes, in substance: `KICKSTART.md` Part 2 is the session prelude (lines 46–80), item 11 installs tools once for all sessions (line 79), item 12 fixes the Firecrawl path once (line 80), and 10(e)'s `SHARED.md` lets agents in a stream reuse each other's partial results (line 72).
*Transfer to the RH program:* none new; recorded as corroboration in §B. The one observation worth keeping: the post's human noticed the repetition by watching the loop "once every couple of hours"; the program's equivalent watch is the harvest, and a repeated setup seen at two consecutive harvests is the trigger to move it into `KICKSTART.md`. Cost: zero.
*Why it may NOT transfer:* no disanalogy; the program's setup is already amortized further than the post's (the prelude is a file, not a person).

### P6. Point out untried directions — and keep a written list of them.
*The page says:* the fourth human role is "pointing out untried directions ('make sure the GPU never blocks on the CPU', 'can you use NVLink SHARP here?')" (What did Devin still need me for?). The post is candid that these were the human's "couple of specific technical insights" and that they came from systems knowledge, not number theory: "I do not understand much of the underlying mathematics" (GNFS optimizations (high-level)).
*What it is, in one sentence:* someone outside the agent's loop holds the list of ideas not yet tried and injects them; the list is distinct from the record of what is known to fail.
*Already adopted here?* **Not on the record** as an artifact. Direction files carry a "Current frontier" written as a contract theorem (10(g), `KICKSTART.md` line 74), and `BARRIER-ZOO.md` records what is blocked, but no file lists per direction the ideas that have never been attempted. The Session 21 digest partly played this role once ("digest §C(iii): CC square, condensed archimedean FF-curve, the Morishita bridge", `STATUS.md` line 119).
*Transfer to the RH program:* add an "Untried" section to each `directions/*.md`: ideas nobody has run, each with the one-line reason it might fit S1–S5 and the rung of the ladder it would be tried on first. Consolidation agents (10(a)) append to it; briefs draw from it; an idea leaves the list only into a result file or a zoo entry. Cost: a file section; the consolidation agent already funded by 10(a) maintains it.
*Why it may NOT transfer:* the post's human could supply the nudges because he knew the *adjacent* domain (GPUs, clusters) well. This program's sponsor has said he is learning the material and is not to be asked technical questions (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, "Do not ask Jay technical questions. Decide, and do it."). The nudging role therefore falls to a second model, which the program already runs as the dual-model rule (standing order 7, `STATUS.md` line 35) and as "an Opus read of its ranking" (`STATUS.md` line 24). The list makes that role concrete; it does not create the outsider the post had.

### P7. Lean on a human-engineered decomposition with a reference implementation; agents lose their footing far from upstream.
*The page says:* "It provided all the relevant techniques, the pipeline stages and their interfaces, and a reference CPU implementation. Using those, I could have the Devin swarm optimize programs roughly independently and compare the outputs with the originals. Like in many other cases, I believe that the human-engineered decomposition of the problem was essential to enabling the agents to make progress" (What did Devin still need me for?). And the warning: "I noticed that the further the codebase got from upstream CADO-NFS, the more confused the agents became. This could be attributed to accumulating complexity, but I wonder whether CADO-NFS's presence in pre-training is also relevant here" (same).
*What it is, in one sentence:* decompose the problem into stages with fixed interfaces and a reference for each, so that agents can work on one stage at a time and check their output against the reference; expect agent reliability to fall with distance from published material.
*Already adopted here?* Partly. 10(b)'s ladder supplies references where RH is known (`KICKSTART.md` line 69); 10(g) fixes interfaces as contract theorems with discharge maps (line 74); 10(f)/(j) compare formal statements against a reviewed statement file (lines 73, 76); the two-producer back-parse cross-check compares two independent outputs "digit-for-digit" (`STATUS.md` line 24). **Not on the record:** the *distance-from-upstream* warning — that verification effort must rise as a construction moves away from named published objects.
*Transfer to the RH program:* for every new definition or object in a Track C construction (`directions/C1-*.md`, `C2-*.md`, `C3-*.md`), the brief requires a one-line "nearest published object" (paper, page) and a statement of exactly how the new object differs; where the answer is "none", the unit is flagged for the dual-model check (standing order 7) before it may be built on. Cost: one line per definition in the direction file; the dual-model check is already funded.
*Why it may NOT transfer — and this is where the disanalogy bites hardest:* the sponsor's charter demands "WHOLLY NEW MACHINERY — potentially a new mathematical field … new objects, axioms, and a master inequality/identity" (`STATUS.md` line 40) and "free rein: build everything, from the axioms up" once the Grossmann sweep is empty (`STATUS.md` line 34). The post says agents are least reliable exactly there. Cognition's answer was to stay close to CADO-NFS; the program cannot. The honest consequence is not to abandon new machinery but to price it correctly: the further from upstream, the more re-derivation per step, the smaller the steps, and the more weight on the rungs where a reference exists. The rule above is that pricing made explicit.

### P8. Verify alongside the main run, at checkpoints, with an independent check — and act when it fires.
*The page says:* "To confirm the correctness of the optimized implementation, which had not been tested on any smaller scale before starting the run, we factored (11^331 - 1)/10 (C344) end-to-end while `krylov` ran. As another check, in parallel with `krylov`, we also ran CADO's `bwccheck` over every V checkpoint pair. CADO's normal in-`krylov` check went off about 14 hours into the run; we re-ran that interval and continued the run correctly" (Appendix 2, Linear algebra). Checkpoint discipline: "We saved checkpoints every 8,192 iterations and kept every fourth one … we deleted the others after verification" (same).
*What it is, in one sentence:* a long computation is checked at every checkpoint by an independent checker while it runs, so that an error costs one interval rather than the run.
*Already adopted here?* Yes for the *end* of a unit: dual blind referees (`STATUS.md` line 30, "duplicated checks, adversarial passes"), the independent Lean checker from a clean clone (10(f), `KICKSTART.md` line 73), the two-producer cross-check (10(j), line 76), and durability checkpoints every ten minutes via the autocommit watchdog (standing order 0, `STATUS.md` line 27). What is **not on the record** is *correctness* checking at intermediate checkpoints of a long computational leg — the watchdog checkpoints for survival, not for truth.
*Transfer to the RH program:* for any computational leg longer than one session slot (Lane A producers, a long Arb sweep), the launch script writes a verifiable checkpoint at fixed intervals and the second producer (or the Lean checker) is run on each checkpoint as it lands, with the result appended to `SHARED.md` (10(e)); a mismatch stops the leg at that interval. Cost: a few lines in the launch script; the checker is already funded as the second producer.
*Why it may NOT transfer:* only the computational arm has checkpoints. A proof has no intermediate state that a checker can validate except a discharged lemma, and the program already checks those (10(g) discharge maps). This practice transfers to D1/Lane A-type legs and to nothing else.

### P9. Keep an honest waste ledger, and publish rejected alternatives with the measured reason.
*The page says:* "643 GPU-days in polynomial selection (this is anomalously high basically due to operator incompetence)" (Cost estimates); "I wasted much search time on unproductive ranges due to incorrect benchmark interpretation … it probably would have been worth it to spend only 12 hours searching less than the intended range" (Appendix 2, Polynomial selection); "It is unclear to me how far we were from optimal overall, but I halted optimization when a 48-hour linear algebra run seemed within reach" (Appendix 2, Linear algebra). Appendix 3 lists, for C337 and C385, the polynomials "rejected by trial sieving" with their measured yields ("octic x^8 - 2 … -55% / -57% / -66% / -71%"), and for C344 alternatives "rejected on norm estimates, not by trial sieving".
*What it is, in one sentence:* the record states what was spent for nothing and why, and every rejected alternative carries the measurement (or the admission that there was none) that rejected it.
*Already adopted here?* Mostly. `LOG.md` is appended "as things land" (standing order 0, `STATUS.md` line 27); record corrections are entered as dated blocks that change no verdict (`STATUS.md` line 24, "32 dated blocks in 14 files, insertion-only"); pricing decisions are written with their reasons (`STATUS.md` line 126, "D-R8 GO … M3 rows NO-GO"); the zoo records what fails and why. **Not on the record:** a per-session *waste line* — what agent budget went to units that produced neither a result nor a zoo entry, and the cause.
*Transfer to the RH program:* the session-close `LOG.md` entry (standing order 2, `STATUS.md` line 29) gains one line: "Spent for nothing: <units>, because <cause>", with the cause drawn from P4's three labels. Over sessions this is the program's own "operator incompetence" line and the input to `KICKSTART.md` amendments. Cost: one line per session; zero agents.
*Why it may NOT transfer:* the post could price waste in GPU-days because every stage had a cost model. The program's waste is in agent slots and sponsor usage, which are not on a shared scale with results; the line can only be qualitative. And a unit that produced no result is not always waste here — a Grossmann scout that finds no fit has done its job (`STATUS.md` line 34). The label must distinguish "found nothing, correctly" from "spent on the wrong thing".

## §A. New rules worth adopting — proposed KICKSTART text, verbatim, NOT applied

The orchestrator adopts or declines. Each is ≤ 8 lines and costs a file, a line, or an already-funded agent; none assumes width.

**(k) Instruments table per direction (from P1).**
Every `directions/*.md` carries an "Instruments" table: the direction's comparable quantities (certified bounds, constants, operating points, zoo/Group-IV counts), their current best value, and the result file that holds it. Briefs instruct agents to report in the table's units and to append a dated row, never to restate. The table records; it never ranks — instruments remain instruments (standing order 4). Consolidation agents (10(a)) reconcile the tables before the digest. (Cognition: "a unified set of measured results, benchmarks, and performance estimators, which evidently were not otherwise going to self-assemble.")

**(l) Dress rehearsal and no-skip clause (amends 10(b), from P2 and P8).**
The ladder also rehearses the *pipeline*: any computational leg or Lean build longer than one session slot first runs end-to-end on a smaller instance of the same shape, and the top rung has been run at target scale before the target starts. A brief that begins the target on a feasibility estimate while a stage is known to be under-verified is returned, as a brief that skips the ladder is. Long legs write verifiable checkpoints at fixed intervals; the second producer or the checker runs on each as it lands and appends to `SHARED.md`; a mismatch stops the leg at that interval. (Cognition skipped the 230-digit rung and its linear algebra "had not been tested on any smaller scale before starting the run"; its checkpoint check "went off about 14 hours into the run".)

**(m) Stop conditions and an Untried list (from P3, P4, P6).**
Every brief carries one line "Stop and report when: …", naming a factual observation (a source found, a number computed, a rung failed) that makes the unit pointless — never an impression. Each `directions/*.md` carries an "Untried" section: ideas not yet attempted, each with its S1–S5 fit reason and its first ladder rung; consolidation agents append, briefs draw, and an idea leaves only into a result file or a zoo entry. At harvest, each abandoned line is labeled (i) obstruction stated and re-derived → zoo candidate, (ii) budget/tool/time → re-queued with the missing input named, or (iii) unexplained → one small re-run before it may be recorded as dead. (Cognition's human roles 1, 2, 4 and 6.)

**(n) Distance-from-upstream line for new machinery (from P7).**
In Track C constructions, every new definition or object carries a one-line "nearest published object" (paper, page) and the exact difference; where the answer is "none", the unit is flagged and passes the dual-model check (standing order 7) before anything is built on it. Steps far from upstream are taken smaller and re-derived more, not avoided — the charter demands new machinery; this rule prices it. (Cognition: "the further the codebase got from upstream CADO-NFS, the more confused the agents became.")

**(o) Waste line at session close (from P9).**
The session-close `LOG.md` entry contains one line "Spent for nothing: <units>, because <cause>", with the cause taken from (m)'s three labels, and distinguishing "found nothing, correctly" (a scout with no fit) from "spent on the wrong thing". The line is the input to `KICKSTART.md` amendments and to the next digest. (Cognition: "643 GPU-days in polynomial selection (this is anomalously high basically due to operator incompetence)".)

## §B. Already ours — where the post corroborates or sharpens an existing rule

- **Ladder rule 10(b)** (`KICKSTART.md` line 69) is the post's "scaling ladder" (Running up the scaling ladder). The post sharpens it with the regretted skipped rung and the untested-at-scale linear algebra → §A(l).
- **Sequential goal ownership** (`STATUS.md` line 31; queue at lines 115–121; Session 21's digest-then-Opus-read-then-first-item order at line 24) is the post's "setting a hierarchy of goals and keeping Devin properly scoped" (What did Devin still need me for?). The program does this with a queue file instead of a person checking "once every couple of hours" (The optimization workflow).
- **Refutation-shaped closes 10(c)** (`KICKSTART.md` line 70) and **no decisive action on unverified claims** (standing order 5, `STATUS.md` line 33) together are the program's answer to "catching when Devin prematurely gave up on a direction"; the post adds only the harvest-side label → §A(m).
- **Independent checker 10(f), Lean shipping 10(j), two-producer cross-check** (`KICKSTART.md` lines 73, 76) are the post's `bwccheck`-over-every-checkpoint and its parallel C344 run (Appendix 2, Linear algebra), applied at unit end rather than at intermediate checkpoints → §A(l).
- **Prelude amortization** (`KICKSTART.md` Part 2 entire; items 11–12 at lines 79–80) is the post's "you can amortize this setup work". Nothing to add.
- **Dual-model review** (standing order 7, `STATUS.md` line 35; "an Opus read of its ranking", line 24) is the program's stand-in for the post's outside-the-loop human who "point[ed] out untried directions" — with the honest difference noted in P6 that the post's human knew the adjacent domain and the sponsor has asked not to be consulted on technical questions.
- **Document as you go** (standing order 0, `STATUS.md` line 27; RULE ONE in `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`) matches the post's checkpoint-and-keep discipline ("We saved checkpoints every 8,192 iterations and kept every fourth one") and its reason for a persistent platform ("sessions can run autonomously for weeks"). The program already assumes the session can die; the post assumed it would not.
- **Honest record** (dated correction blocks, `STATUS.md` line 24; pricing with reasons, line 126) matches the post's "operator incompetence" and "incorrect benchmark interpretation" admissions; the post's rejected-polynomial tables with measured yields (Appendix 3, C337/C385) are the shape the zoo's entries already take ("proof class X cannot yield Y because Z", 10(c)).

## §C. Explicitly NOT to copy

As the NS study refused width (`KICKSTART.md` line 78: "Ten thousand agents is not a technique, it is a budget"), this study refuses the following, each with the post's own words for what it was.

1. **Width and agent-spawned children.** "an average of 3 and a maximum of 18 concurrent Devin sessions"; "Devins themselves started 101 child sessions" (The optimization workflow; What did Devin still need me for?). Standing order 3-amended: "one workflow at a time … at most two agents run side by side" (`STATUS.md` line 31), because "Three usage-limit deaths in one day each killed ten or more agents in flight". The post's platform did not have that failure mode ("sessions are persistent and independent from my computer"); the program's does.
2. **Overlapping phases and co-optimizing against speculative targets.** "We optimized the linear algebra while sieving proceeded. Optimization was turbulent because we simultaneously co-optimized matrix params, solver layout, and code targeting speculative final matrix properties … This fed back into sieving … nudged the relation target a couple of times" (Appendix 2, Linear algebra). The program's sequential streams (`KICKSTART.md` line 55) are the deliberate opposite; the turbulence the post reports is the cost it paid for overlap, and the program cannot afford to lose an overlapped stream to a usage death.
3. **Starting the target on an estimate before the pipeline is verified.** "I estimated that RSA-260 could be done in under a month and therefore had already begun polynomial selection, even though I knew the linear algebra remained significantly underoptimized" (Running up the scaling ladder). 10(b) returns such a brief (`KICKSTART.md` line 69); §A(l) says so in words.
4. **"Just programming" as a direction.** "if a problem can be solved via 'just programming', it seems worthwhile to attempt this immediately" (Assorted reflections). The post itself reports "essentially no algorithmic advancements" (How did this happen?). RH is not a computation; the program's computational arm (D1, `directions/D1-certified-refutation-arm.md`) exists as an instrument under standing order 4 ("density/proportion work is instruments only", `STATUS.md` line 32), and the sponsor's charter is new machinery (`STATUS.md` line 40). The overhang the post describes is real for pipelines with a reference implementation; the program has none for its headline track.
5. **Operating at "car hobbyist" understanding.** "I do not understand much of the underlying mathematics" (GNFS optimizations (high-level)) — workable when the answer checks itself by multiplication. In this program the sponsor is reading to learn (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`), the deliverable is understanding embodied in a proof or a certified obstruction, and the post itself names the risk: "I share some concerns about a loss of human understanding" (Assorted reflections). The program's plain-English reporting rule and the zoo-as-asset stance are the answer; nothing from the post's understanding model is to be copied.
6. **Reallocating by feel.** The post's polynomial-selection search "was irregular and a bit ad-hoc; … Search parameters shifted as benchmark results were produced" (Appendix 2, Polynomial selection) — the post's own account of what the missing benchmark framework cost. 10(d) reallocates only on a graded result "above threshold" (`KICKSTART.md` line 71); keep it that way.

## §D. What the post says about the sponsor's lean-budget constraint

The post's cost is two-sided and the two sides scale differently. Compute: "about 4,900 GPU-days … about $400k at current market prices" (Cost estimates), at "no marginal cost" because it ran on "spare or fragmented compute" (Factoring on spare compute) — a resource the program does not have and does not need, since its computational arm runs on one MacBook under a four-heavy-job cap (`KICKSTART.md` lines 57–58). Steering: "82,702 words … in 3,328 messages across 192 sessions out of 233 used for factoring (totaling 14,450 ACUs)", with the human present "once every couple of hours" for three weeks (What did Devin still need me for?; The optimization workflow). The post's own accounting says where the money was lost: 643 of 4,923 GPU-days (about 13%) went to polynomial selection that was "anomalously high basically due to operator incompetence", traced to "incorrect benchmark interpretation" and to a ladder rung skipped on an estimate — steering failures, not compute failures. That is the transferable fact for a program whose regime is "one workflow at a time … at most two agents" (`STATUS.md` line 31) under a usage cap that can end a session without warning (`STATUS.md` line 27): the post's waste came from the parts of its process that the program's lean regime already forces it to do carefully (one goal at a time, harvest before the next stream), and the post's single largest contribution by its own account — the benchmarking framework "which evidently were not otherwise going to self-assemble" — costs a file, not an agent. The sponsor's sentence "we must be really smart about directions to pursue" (`KICKSTART.md` line 67) is, in the post's vocabulary, "set priorities, establish benchmarks, and recognize when work was going off-track" (opening, takeaway 2); the post spent 13% of a $400k budget learning that the second of those must come first. Nothing in the post argues for more agents in flight; its 18-session peak is what the human "could barely keep up with" (Running up the scaling ladder), and its 36 unattended sessions out of 233 are the exception it reports, not the rule.
